readings.title: The Sun Stands Still
readings.subtitle: The Defeat of the Amorite Coalition
readings.text: [Joshua 10:1] And it came to be when Adoni-Tsedeq king of Yerushalayim heard how Yehoshua had captured Ai and had put it under the ban – as he had done to Yeriḥo and its sovereign, so he had done to Ai and its sovereign – and how the inhabitants of Gib‛on had made peace with Yisra’el and were among them, [2] that they feared greatly, because Gib‛on was a great city, like one of the royal cities, and because it was greater than Ai, and all its men were mighty. [3] So Adoni-Tsedeq king of Yerushalayim sent to Hoham king of Ḥebron, and to Pir’am king of Yarmuth, and to Yaphi‘a king of Lakhish, and to Debir king of Eglon, saying, [4] “Come up to me and help me, and let us smite Gib‛on, for it has made peace with Yehoshua and with the children of Yisra’el.” [5] And the five sovereigns of the Amorites, the king of Yerushalayim, the king of Ḥebron, the king of Yarmuth, the king of Lakhish, the king of Eglon, gathered together and went up, they and all their camps, and camped before Gib‛on and fought against it. [6] And the men of Gib‛on sent to Yehoshua at the camp at Gilgal, saying, “Do not withdraw your hand from your servants. Come up to us quickly and save us and help us, for all the sovereigns of the Amorites who dwell in the mountains have assembled against us.” [7] And Yehoshua went up from Gilgal, he and all the people of war with him, and all the mighty brave men. [8] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Yehoshua, <dq>“Do not be afraid of them, for <dn>I</dn> have given them into your hand. Not a man of them stands before you.”</dq> [9] And Yehoshua came upon them suddenly, having gone up from Gilgal all night. [10] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> confused them before Yisra’el, and smote them with a great slaughter at Gib‛on, and pursued them by the way of the ascent of Beyth Ḥoron, and smote them as far as Azěqah and Maqqědah. [11] And it came to be, as they fled before Yisra’el and were on the descent of Beyth Ḥoron, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> threw down large stones from the heavens on them as far as Azěqah, and they died. There were more who died from the hailstones than the children of Yisra’el killed with the sword. [12] Then Yehoshua spoke to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in the day when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave the Amorites over to the children of Yisra’el, and he said before the eyes of Yisra’el, “Sun, stand still over Gib‛on; and Moon, in the Valley of Ayalon.” [13] So the sun stood still, and the moon stopped, till the nation avenged itself upon their enemies. Is this not written in the Book of Yashar? Thus the sun stood in the midst of the heavens, and did not hasten to go down for a whole day. [14] And there has been no day like that, before it or after it, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> listened to the voice of a man, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> fought for Yisra’el. [15] Then Yehoshua returned, and all Yisra’el with him, to the camp at Gilgal.

readings.title: Judgment at Makkedah
readings.subtitle: The Execution of the Five Kings
readings.text: [Joshua 10:16] But these five sovereigns had fled and hidden themselves in a cave at Maqqědah. [17] And it was reported to Yehoshua, saying, “The five sovereigns have been found hidden in the cave at Maqqědah.” [18] And Yehoshua said, “Roll large stones against the mouth of the cave, and set men by it to guard them. [19] “But do not stay there yourselves, pursue your enemies, and attack their rear guard. Do not allow them to enter their cities, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has given them into your hand.” [20] And it came to be, when Yehoshua and the children of Yisra’el had ended smiting them with a very great slaughter, till they had finished, that those who remained of them entered into the walled cities. [21] And all the people returned to the camp, to Yehoshua at Maqqědah, in peace. No one moved his tongue against any of the children of Yisra’el. [22] And Yehoshua said, “Open the mouth of the cave, and bring out those five sovereigns to me from the cave.” [23] And they did so, and brought out those five sovereigns to him from the cave: the king of Yerushalayim, the king of Ḥebron, the king of Yarmuth, the king of Lakhish, the king of Eglon. [24] And it came to be, when they brought out those sovereigns to Yehoshua, that Yehoshua called for all the men of Yisra’el, and said to the chiefs of the men of war who went with him, “Come near, put your feet on the necks of these sovereigns.” And they came near and put their feet on their necks. [25] And Yehoshua said to them, “Do not be afraid, nor be discouraged. Be strong and courageous, for this is what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is going to do to all your enemies against whom you fight.” [26] And afterward Yehoshua smote them and killed them, and hanged them on five trees. And they were hanging on the trees until evening. [27] And it came to be at the time of the going down of the sun that Yehoshua commanded, and they took them down from the trees, and threw them into the cave where they had been hidden, and laid large stones against the cave’s mouth, to this day.

readings.title: The Southern Campaign
readings.subtitle: Conquest of the Hill Country and Negeb
readings.text: [Joshua 10:28] And Yehoshua captured Maqqědah on that day, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and its sovereign. He put them under the ban, all the beings who were in it. He let no survivor remain. And he did to the sovereign of Maqqědah as he had done to the sovereign of Yeriḥo. [29] And Yehoshua passed from Maqqědah, and all Yisra’el with him, to Libnah, and fought against Libnah. [30] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave it also, and its sovereign, into the hand of Yisra’el. And he smote it with the edge of the sword, and all the beings who were in it. He let no survivor remain in it. And he did to its sovereign as he had done to the sovereign of Yeriḥo. [31] And Yehoshua passed from Libnah, and all Yisra’el with him, to Lakhish, and encamped against it and fought against it. [32] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave Lakhish into the hand of Yisra’el, and he captured it on the second day, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and all the beings who were in it, according to all that he had done to Libnah. [33] Then Horam sovereign of Gezer came up to help Lakhish, and Yehoshua smote him and his people, until he let no survivor remain. [34] And Yehoshua passed from Lakhish, and all Yisra’el with him, to Eglon, and they encamped against it and fought against it. [35] And they captured it on that day, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and all the beings who were in it he put under the ban on that day, according to all that he had done to Lakhish. [36] And Yehoshua went up from Eglon, and all Yisra’el with him, to Ḥebron, and they fought against it. [37] And they captured it and smote it with the edge of the sword, and its sovereign, and all its cities, and all the beings who were in it. He let no survivor remain, according to all that he had done to Eglon, but put it under the ban, and all the beings who were in it. [38] And Yehoshua returned, and all Yisra’el with him, to Debir, and fought against it. [39] And he captured it and its sovereign and all its cities, and they smote them with the edge of the sword and put under the ban all the beings who were in it. He let no survivor remain. As he had done to Ḥebron, so he did to Debir and its sovereign, as he had done also to Libnah and its sovereign. [40] Thus Yehoshua smote all the land: the mountain country and the South and the low country and the slopes, and all their sovereigns. He let no survivor remain, but put under the ban all that breathed, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’el had commanded. [41] And Yehoshua smote them from Qaděsh Barnea as far as Azzah, and all the country of Goshen, even as far as Gib‛on. [42] And all these sovereigns and their land Yehoshua captured at one time, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’el fought for Yisra’el. [43] Then Yehoshua returned, and all Yisra’el with him, to the camp at Gilgal.

readings.title: The Northern Campaign
readings.subtitle: Victory at the Waters of Merom
readings.text: [Joshua 11:1] And it came to be, when Yabin sovereign of Ḥatsor heard, that he sent to Yobab sovereign of Madon, and to the sovereign of Shimron, and to the sovereign of Akhshaph, [2] and to the sovereigns who were from the north, in the mountains, and in the desert south of Kinneroth, and in the low country, and in the heights of Dor on the west, [3] to the Kena‛anite in the east and in the west, and the Amorite, and the Ḥittite, and the Perizzite, and the Yebusite in the mountains, and the Ḥivvite below Ḥermon in the land of Mitspah. [4] And they went out, they and all their camps with them, a people as many as the sand on the seashore in number, with very many horses and chariots. [5] And all these sovereigns met together, and they came and camped together at the waters of Merom to fight against Yisra’el. [6] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Yehoshua, <dq>“Do not be afraid of them, for tomorrow about this time <dn>I</dn> am giving all of them slain before Yisra’el. You shall hamstring their horses and burn their chariots with fire.”</dq> [7] And Yehoshua, and all the people of war with him, came against them suddenly by the waters of Merom, and they fell upon them. [8] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave them into the hand of Yisra’el, and they smote them and pursued them to Great Tsidon, and to Misrephoth Mayim, and to the Valley of Mitspeh eastward. And they smote them until they let no survivor remain to them. [9] And Yehoshua did to them as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had said to him: he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire. [10] And Yehoshua turned back at that time and captured Ḥatsor, and smote its sovereign with the sword, for Ḥatsor was formerly the head of all those reigns. [11] And they smote all the beings who were in it with the edge of the sword, putting them under the ban. Not one breathing being was left. And he burned Ḥatsor with fire. [12] And Yehoshua captured all the cities of those sovereigns, and all their sovereigns, and he smote them with the edge of the sword. He put them under the ban, as Mosheh the servant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded. [13] However, Yisra’el did not burn any cities that stood on their mounds, except Ḥatsor only, which Yehoshua burned. [14] And all the spoil of these cities and the livestock, the children of Yisra’el took as booty for themselves. But they smote every man with the edge of the sword until they had destroyed them, and they did not leave any breathing being. [15] As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded Mosheh <dn>His</dn> servant, so Mosheh commanded Yehoshua, and so Yehoshua did. He did not turn aside a word of all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded Mosheh. [16] Thus Yehoshua took all this land: the mountain country, and all the South, and all the land of Goshen, and the low country, and the desert plain, and the mountains of Yisra’el and its low lands, [17] from Mount Ḥalaq that goes up to Se‛ir, even as far as Ba‛al Gad in the Valley of Lebannon below Mount Ḥermon. And he captured all their sovereigns, and smote them and killed them. [18] Yehoshua made war a long time with all those sovereigns. [19] There was not a city that made peace with the children of Yisra’el, except the Ḥivvites, the inhabitants of Gib‛on. They took all in battle. [20] For it was of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to harden their hearts, that they should come against Yisra’el in battle, in order that <dn>He</dn> might put them under the ban, that they might have no favour, but that <dn>He</dn> might destroy them, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded Mosheh. [21] And at that time Yehoshua came and cut off the Anaqim from the mountains: from Ḥebron, from Debir, from Anab, and from all the mountains of Yehudah, and from all the mountains of Yisra’el. Yehoshua put them under the ban with their cities. [22] There were no Anaqim left in the land of the children of Yisra’el; only in Azzah, in Gath, and in Ashdod some remained. [23] So Yehoshua took all the land, according to all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had said to Mosheh. And Yehoshua gave it as an inheritance to Yisra’el according to their divisions by their tribes. And the land rested from war.

readings.title: Kings East of the Jordan
readings.subtitle: The Conquests of Mosheh
readings.text: [Joshua 12:1] And these are the sovereigns of the land whom the children of Yisra’el smote, and whose land they possessed beyond the Yarden toward the rising of the sun, from the wadi Arnon to Mount Ḥermon, and all the desert plain eastward: [2] Siḥon sovereign of the Amorites, who dwelt in Ḥeshbon and ruled from Aro‛er, which is on the bank of the wadi Arnon, and from the middle of that wadi, and half Gil‛ad, even as far as the wadi Yabboq, which is the border of the children of Ammon, [3] and the desert plain from the Sea of Kinneroth eastward as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, the way of Beyth Yeshimoth, and southward below the slopes of Pisgah. [4] And the border of Og sovereign of Bashan, who was of the remnant of the Repha’im, who dwelt at Ashtaroth and at Edre‛i, [5] and ruled in Mount Ḥermon, and in Salḵah, and in all Bashan, as far as the border of the Geshurite and the Ma‛aḵathite, and the half of Gil‛ad the border of Siḥon sovereign of Ḥeshbon. [6] Mosheh the servant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and the children of Yisra’el had smitten them. And Mosheh the servant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave it as a possession to the Re’ubenites, and to the Gadites, and to half the tribe of Menashsheh.
